changed_sentences.why: English 'starts now', Arabic «تبدأ الآن». With the habitual present «شروع ہوتا ہے» Urdu says «اب» ('now'); «ابھی» ('this very moment / just now') goes with a perfective or an imperative («ابھی شروع ہوا ہے», «ابھی شروع کریں») and beside the habitual it reads as the English adverb carried over. The heading keeps its meaning, its word order and its length. Reviewer's judgement, not a count: ur.wikipedia has no hit for either phrase («اب شروع ہوتا ہے» 0, «ابھی شروع ہوتا ہے» 0).

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: دنیا کے سب سے بڑے نخلستان کا سیاحتی رہنما
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'Travel Guide to the World’s Largest Oasis', AR «دليلك السياحي لأكبر واحة في العالم». The site's claim as both sources make it, with neither 'palm' nor 'natural' (C15). The brand that leads the English and Arabic titles is not written (DECISIONS: do what ru / de / zh do on this key — they lead with the destination).

AR «دليل سياحة الأحساء» says 'tourism guide'; EN 'Your guide to Al-Ahsa'. Stage 2 dropped the address word 'your' (the Arabic and Russian values carry none) and took «سیاحتی» from the Arabic: no fact enters or leaves.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: یونیسکو کے عالمی ورثے میں شامل اس نخلستان
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'the UNESCO-listed oasis', AR «واحة مسجلة في تراث اليونسكو العالمي». 'World Heritage' is the Arabic's wording made explicit; nothing beyond the listing is said.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: 2.5 ملین سے زیادہ کھجور کے درختوں
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'more than 2.5 million date palms', AR «أكثر من 2.5 مليون نخلة». Digits and scale exactly as the sources (open item P10 is raised, not applied). The palm word stands in the second sentence, the largest-oasis claim in the first (C15).
EN '“Al-Ahsa” is the plural of “hisy”', AR «جمعُ «حِسْي»». «لفظ» ('the word') only marks the quoted item as a word under discussion; it names no language and adds no fact.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: ہاتھ سے ریت ہٹائیں تو پھوٹ نکلتا ہے
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: AR «تكشفه يدُك فلا يلبث أن يفور» ('your hand uncovers it'); EN 'brush it away and it springs up'. «ہاتھ سے» is the Arabic's hand, not an addition.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: سب یہیں کے لوگوں کے ہاتھوں سے
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'From harvesting dates to embroidering cloaks by local hands', AR «من قطف التمر إلى تطريز البشوت بأيدي أهلها». In both sources 'by local hands' can be read with the whole range; «سب» says that reading aloud. Logged as a source ambiguity (ru and de attach it to the cloaks only); the literal fallback is «کھجوریں توڑنے سے لے کر یہیں کے لوگوں کے ہاتھوں چغوں پر کڑھائی تک۔».

EN 'A warm kitchen', AR «مطبخٌ دافئ». An evaluative word, not a fact (P19): the warmth of the source said with the Urdu image of the spread instead of the room. No dish, no claim is added; the four dishes are the source's four.
EN 'the gleam of gold and copper'; AR «والذهب والنحاس» has no word for gleam. Evaluative wording taken from the English (P19), no claim.

EN 'Al-Qaisariyah' / 'Qaisariyah Souq', AR «القيصرية» / «سوق القيصرية». One name, one form (P1): the card line writes the full name where the English shortens it, as the ru, de and zh values of the same key do.
A superlative needs the Arabic (P19): AR «أبرزُ معالم الواحة», EN 'foremost landmarks'.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: قدیم ترین داستانوں میں سے ایک
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: AR «واحدةً من أقدم حكايات الإسلام», EN 'one of the oldest stories in Islam': the superlative and its hedge ('one of') both stand in both sources.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: دنیا کا سب سے بڑا نخلستان
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'the largest oasis on earth', AR «أكبر واحةٍ في العالم». The source's dash is a sentence break in the Urdu so that the palm word stays out of the sentence that carries the claim (C15, ruling P25); two fragments, no final stop.
EN 'barracks', AR «الثكنات»: the plain Urdu for the thing (soldiers' quarters) instead of the loan. Nothing is said about the building that the source does not say; 'one wall' is «ایک ہی فصیل».
EN 'Green groves'; AR «خضرةٌ» ('greenery'). The Urdu follows the English noun; logged as a small divergence of the sources, no claim.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: وسط جون سے اگست کے آخر تک
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'from mid-June to the end of August', AR «من منتصف يونيو إلى نهاية أغسطس». The season exactly as given; no advice about heat or hours is added (stage 3 logged the temptation).

EN 'arrows to move', AR «الأسهم للتنقّل». Urdu has no bare intransitive for moving a selection; in the result list the movement is up and down, and that is what the arrow keys do in Search.astro. It describes the same key action, promises nothing more; the literal alternative is «تیر کے نشانوں سے آگے پیچھے جائیں».

EN 'Skip to content', AR «تخطَّ إلى المحتوى»; de and zh say 'main content' for the same link. The target is the page's main landmark, so the label says no more than its target. Urdu sites word the same link «مواد پر جائیں» (BBC Urdu, DW) and «مرکزی مواد پر جائیں» (VOA).

EN 'From the place', AR «من المكان»: a gallery heading. The Urdu names what the section holds, as the approved ru («Фотографии этого места») and de («Fotos vom Ort») values do; the section holds photographs of the place and nothing else, so the label promises exactly its target.
EN 'Visit information', AR «معلومات الزيارة». Calibration candidate read in place by three blind readers without remark (P27). It names the reader instead of the act; the card under it is unchanged.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: اس لیے جانے سے پہلے {op} سے تصدیق کر لیں
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'confirm with {op} before visiting', AR «تأكد من {op} قبل الزيارة». «اس لیے» renders the source's dash as a consequence; no condition is added to the notice.

EN 'the operator', AR «المشغّل». Stage 3 replaced «وہاں کی» with «اس مقام کی»: the operator of the place the page is about is what the source means, and who that is the source still does not say (calibration source defect SD14). No name, no office, no telephone is added.

EN 'Complete your day', AR «أكمل يومك», de «Den Tag abrunden». Stage 2 replaced «مکمل کریں», which reads 'finish your day' in Urdu; 'make it full' is the source's sense and makes no promise about the day.
EN 'No matching attractions yet', AR «لا توجد معالم مطابقة بعد». Urdu must say what the places match; the line shows only when the page's own search box has filtered every card away.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: اس ویب سائٹ کو یہ جاننے کی اجازت
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'check the browser’s location permission', AR «تحقق من إذن الموقع في المتصفح». KEPT WITH A LOSS, raised as item N4: it is the same permission (the one the browser gives this site), but 'in the browser' — where to look — is not said, because the only Urdu word for it is a loan with no dictionary headword (P16). Nothing is added; one detail of the source is missing.

fence_checked_and_kept.phrase: یہ ویب سائٹ ایک آزاد سیاحتی رہنما ہے
fence_checked_and_kept.why_it_is_in_the_source: EN 'Visit Al-Ahsa is an independent visitor guide', AR «زوروا الأحساء موقع إرشادي مستقل». The brand is replaced by 'this site' (raised as item N1); independence, 'not a government body' and 'does not represent any official authority' all stand, none is strengthened.

EN 'My saved places', AR «معالمي المحفوظة». Stage 2 added «کردہ» so that the participle can only mean 'saved' (bare «محفوظ مقامات» is the set phrase for protected sites: 208 pages on ur.wikipedia). Same three ideas as the source.
EN 'Restaurants & Cafés', AR «المطاعم والمقاهي». Places to eat and to drink: the two kinds of the source said with native words; the label does not narrow or widen what the section lists.
EN 'Not to be missed', AR «معالم لا تُفوَّت». The same recommendation, said positively; no superlative.
EN 'Why Al-Ahsa', AR «لماذا الأحساء». The particle is how Urdu asks 'why this place (and not another)'; it adds emphasis, not content.

candidates: A — digits and scale as the source: «2.5 ملین سے زیادہ» (in the text, both strings)
B — the Urdu scale: «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ» (the digits change: 2.5 million = 25 lakh)
C — the Urdu scale in words: «پچیس لاکھ سے زیادہ» (no digit at all; not proposed for the figure card)
open_items.evidence: First text that tests the item. PRESS, the reader's own paper, on this very figure: urdunews.com/node/510071 (9 Oct 2020) «الاحسا میں 25 لاکھ سے زیادہ کھجوروں کے درخت ہیں»; node/891678 (1 Jul 2025) «20 لاکھ کے قریب کھجوروں کے درخت ہیں جن سے سالانہ 120 ہزار ٹن …»; node/895742 (12 Oct 2025) «صرف الاحسا میں ہی کھجور کے ڈھائی لاکھ درخت ہیں» beside «سعودی عرب میں کھجور کے 33 ملین درخت ہیں» — lakh three times for the palms of Al-Ahsa, «ملین» once, for the national figure (all three pages fetched and read in this run; the third figure, 'two and a half lakh', is the paper's own slip and is quoted as written). REFERENCE: ur.wikipedia exact phrases «25 لاکھ» 82 pages against «2.5 ملین» 58; «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ» 3 against «2.5 ملین سے زیادہ» 5; «لاکھ سے زیادہ» 322 against «ملین سے زیادہ» 404 — both scales are alive in the reference corpus. DICTIONARY: Urdu Lughat (udb.gov.pk result list) has the headword «مِلیَن» and defines it as «دس لاکھ»: the loan is a dictionary word, explained through the native scale. PRECEDENT inside the site: the Chinese value of the same two strings converts to its native scale with other digits («250 多万»); ru and de keep 2.5 with their own scale word. COST of B: the digits differ from the source, so the stage checker's number probe (every figure of the Urdu must stand in a source) fires until it learns the conversion; the figure card, the hero lead and the JSON-LD description that repeats the hero lead change together.
open_items.recommendation: B, «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ», ruled together with a conversion test in the checker (million → 10 lakh, 10 million → 1 crore; thousands as the source): it is how the reader's paper writes this very fact, it is the native scale, and the Chinese line already set the precedent of a native scale with different digits. Until the judge rules, the text keeps the source's digits («2.5 ملین سے زیادہ») as the provisional rule says. The figure card and the hero lead must carry the same form.

notes.text: Stage 2, nine changes. (1) inline.home.description «الاحساء کے لیے آپ کا رہنما:» → «الاحساء کا سیاحتی رہنما:» — the address word goes, 'tourism' comes from the Arabic («دليل سياحة الأحساء»): meaning kept. (2) search.placeholder «کوئی مقام» → «سیاحتی مقام» — 'sights', kept. (3) nav.myTrip and (4) home.route.link «محفوظ» → «محفوظ کردہ» — 'saved', disambiguated, kept. (5) home.name.body «کوئی اس کی توقع نہیں کرتا» → «کسی کو اس کی توقع نہیں ہوتی» — same clause, kept. (6) cat.historic.d and (7) CATEGORY_LABELS.religious «مسجدیں» → «مساجد» — a plural form, kept. (8) map.locate.err rewritten without the noun «مقام» — what failed and which permission are both still said; the browser was already missing at stage 1. (9) det.nearby.h «مکمل کریں» → «بھرپور بنائیں» — 'complete your day' in the sense of rounding it out, kept. Stage 3, two changes. (10) det.hoursNotice.op «وہاں کی انتظامیہ» → «اس مقام کی انتظامیہ» — the same operator, now said of the place; no fact. (11) search.placeholder reordered with the verb first — the same four content words. All eleven kept the meaning; none promises more than the English or the Arabic.

notes.item: native wording against the common loan: the finding, label by label
notes.text: The owner's rule is about common equivalents. CONFIRMED common for the function, with evidence in the verification log: «تلاش» / «تلاش کریں» (search: four news sites and MediaWiki), «صفحہ اول» (home: Urdu News, Geo, VOA; BBC and Express write it with the izafat sign, which ruling P8 drops), «محفوظ کریں» (save: MediaWiki), «زمرہ» (category: MediaWiki), «عجائب گھر» (museums: 3152 pages against the loan's 2768, and a dictionary headword), «تفریح گاہیں» (parks: the dictionary defines the loan by it), «قیام گاہیں» (places to stay: used of tourist lodging), «تقریبات», «پکوان», «نقشہ», «ہم سے رابطہ کریں» (BBC, Dawn, Geo), «شرائط و ضوابط» (Dawn's footer). ATTESTED for the function but rarer than the loan: «فہرست» for a menu, «ربط … نقل ہو گیا» for a copied link (both MediaWiki), «کھانے پینے کی جگہیں» for places to eat — item N6. NOT what Urdu sites call the thing: «مضامین» for the blog (sites say «بلاگ», which no dictionary heads) — item N6; «دوسروں کو بھیجیں» for share — item N3; «کھیت» for farms one visits — item N5. Nothing in the batch is a coined purism; three wordings are descriptions where the everyday word is a loan the rule keeps out.

notes.item: loans in the text and their entries (ruling P16)
notes.text: In the text with an entry that cites P16: «ویب سائٹ» (verified, two dictionaries), «آن لائن» (verified, one entry page), «ویڈیو» (gender verified, spelling pending), the brands «گوگل میپس» (termbase) and «واٹس ایپ» (verified), and the termbase's «فیس». The scale word «ملین» is not treated as a loan to admit: it stands by the provisional rule of open item P10 (digits and scale as the source) and is itself a headword of Urdu Lughat. The unit «کلومیٹر» follows the style rule for units (one word: 65588 pages against 2385 for the spaced form). The key name 'Enter' is Latin by the pack's allowance. Kept out and raised: «شیئر», «براؤزر», «بلاگ», «لنک», «مینو», «ریستوراں», «کیفے», «فارم», «پارک», «ہوٹل».

No blind reader will see either; this stage read them letter by letter and the proofreader does so again. «سعودی عرب»: seen, ain, waw, dal, yeh U+06CC, space, ain, reh, beh — the reference title. «الاحساء کا نخلستان»: alif, lam, plain alif (P11), hah, seen, alif, final hamza (P2), space, kaf U+06A9, alif, space, noon, khah, lam, seen, teh, alif, noon — the possessive ruling P8 gives, attested in the press with the paper's own head-name form.

«ڈھلتی سہ پہر» is kept: it is the only candidate that keeps 'late' (AR «آخر العصر»). It has no hit on ur.wikipedia, nor has «سہ پہر ڈھلے»; «پچھلے پہر», weighed here, means the last watch of the night and was dropped. Bare «سہ پہر» (139 pages) is the fallback if the blind reader finds the participle odd on a time pill; the prayer names stay out, as stage 3 decided.

«سیاحتی رہنما» (page title, description, list.eyebrow, footer line) is kept: «گائیڈ» is on the banned list, and «رہنما» is the batch's word. On ur.wikipedia the phrase is a person in four pages of five; for a site that calls itself a guide the personal reading does no harm, but it is why stage 2 moved the description away from «آپ کا رہنما». Not a fence matter; for the blind reader.

The twelve carried from stages 1 to 3 stand. Added: (13) map.locate.err — both sources say 'in the browser'; the Urdu cannot (item N4). (14) fact.palms.l and home.hero.lead — the sources' own figure, 2.5 million, is 'more than 25 lakh' in the reader's paper and 'close to 20 lakh' in a later report of the same paper: the site's figure is the owner's, and nothing is changed. (15) det.fromPlace — 'From the place' / «من المكان» does not say what the section holds in either source; the Urdu, like ru and de, does.

Read letter by letter: inline.home.country and data.oasisName. Agreement to check against the entries returned here: «ویب سائٹ» feminine, «ویڈیو» feminine, «مسجد» feminine (plural «مساجد» with a feminine verb), «ورثہ» masculine, «بندرگاہ» feminine by usage (pending), «خلیج» feminine (not exercised), «انتظامیہ» feminine, «ربط» masculine («نقل ہو گیا»), «لیموں» and «باغ» masculine. Labels and headings carry no final stop; fact.palms.l has a stop inside and none at the end. The one string this stage changed is a heading. Two things seen on the dictionary pages while the names were being settled, left for the proof pass because they are orthography and agreement, not benchmarking: the headword of the word for a layer is «تَہ», and home.name.body writes it with a second heh; and the entry page of «کھجور» prints masculine while cat.crafts.d has the feminine plural «کھجوریں», which is also what the dictionary's own idioms and the press write.

No entry page of Urdu Lughat could be opened (the site failed from the 27th request on): what is cited from it is the result list, which prints headword and definition but no gender. The gender of «بندرگاہ» therefore rests on usage against one printed label, and stays pending. Genders of «سعودی عرب», «یونیسکو», «العقیر», «واٹس ایپ», «ہریس», «مفلق» are formal: no dictionary lists a name, and none is exercised in this batch. That the search box of the Rekhta dictionary misses existing entries was shown for four words; its silence on «شیئر», «براؤزر», «بلاگ» is therefore weak evidence, and for these three the stronger evidence is the missing English-headword pages and the empty Urdu Lughat search — a headword under another spelling cannot be excluded. That commercial interfaces label the share button «اشتراک کریں» is recollection: the Urdu help pages tried answered in English. Counts are ur.wikipedia exact-phrase page counts of today: forms and frequency, never style. Nothing was measured on a build. The one text change rests on the reviewer's judgement of Urdu usage, with no count behind it.
